source: J. S. Barrowman, The Practical Calculation of the Aerodynamic Characteristics of Slender Finned Vehicles, MS thesis, The Catholic University of America, 1967 (NASA/TM-2001-209983): Fig. 5-6, the Basic Finner (printed p. 69, PDF p. 79), and Fig. 5-7, its roll damping derivative, theory and wind tunnel (printed p. 70, PDF p. 80). The wind-tunnel points are from Barrowman's reference 21, J. D. Nicolaides, Missile Flight and Astrodynamics, BuWeps TN-100A, 1959 (a US Navy report), which he says does not state their accuracy. US Government work.
reading: Read from a 300-dpi render of Fig. 5-7 with its grid calibrated between the nearest ticks (the axis's last interval, Mach 2.5 to 3.0, is drawn 285 px long against about 235 px for the others): each wind-tunnel symbol's centre, +-0.3 in C_lp and +-0.01 in Mach (the points at Mach 2.27 and 3.00 touch the theory curve and were read by hand); and the theory curve at Mach 0.07, where it is flat. The figure gives A_r = 78.6 in^2 and L_r = 10 in, the body's cross-section and diameter, so C_lp is per unit of p L_r/(2V) (Barrowman eq. 3-49). Read 2026-09-19 (M1.8c).

geometry.note: Fig. 5-6, in calibers of the body diameter D: a body 10 D long from the nose tip with a conical nose (marked 20 deg), four square fins D in chord and D in span at the base (3 D tip to tip), wedge sections 8% of D thick plus the leading edge's thickness.

wind_tunnel_note: Disputed (issue #763): these points sit a flat 1.27 times BRL 799's range curve as NAVORD 6652 Fig. 7 replots it (docs/research/nicolaides-roll-damping-convention.md section 3), which fits a convention slip in Barrowman's reference 21, not an aerodynamic difference, and 1.21 to 1.26 times DREV-TM-9703's range fits. Kept as Barrowman printed them; the scored reference is nol_tunnel_c_lp.
nol_tunnel_source: F. J. Regan, Roll Damping Moment Measurements for the Basic Finner at Subsonic and Supersonic Speeds, NAVORD Report 6652 (Aerodynamics Research Report 59), US Naval Ordnance Laboratory, 20 March 1964 (DTIC AD0600975): Table 2, 'Summary of supersonic roll damping data at zero angle of attack' (PDF p. 17), the average column; spin decay in a wind tunnel at 50 to 150 rps, angle of attack 0. Table 2 prints the fifth row's Mach as 2.70, Table 1 (PDF p. 16) as 2.76; 2.76 is used. US Government work, released without restrictions.
nol_tunnel_conversion: NAVORD 6652 defines the coefficient as L/(q A_p b n) per p b/(2V), with A_p one panel, b the 3 d fin span and n the fin count (PDF p. 6; the same as BRL Report 711's). With A_p = d^2 and n = 4, multiplying by A_p n b^2/(pi d^4/4) = 144/pi = 45.84 gives C_lp per p d/(2V) on pi d^2/4, negative for damping. ARL-TR-846 Table 7 lists BRL 711's values so converted, and AEDC-TR-76-58 Fig. 9b plots NOL's Mach 2.5 point near -16, which confirms the factor (docs/research/finner-reference-data.md section 1).
